verdicts.summary: The release-time roster clear mostly holds up. The byte-for-byte round-trip risk is already finding 0. One extra hazard I could not confirm or rule out: every clear write is a `provider-thread.updated` event, and the projection reducer uses that event to move the app thread's `activeProviderThreadId`.
evidence: apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:857-873 (the clear writes `provider-thread.updated` for each captured provider thread, not only the active one)
apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts:2249-2276 (any `provider-thread.updated` with a non-null appThreadId sets `thread.activeProviderThreadId = event.payload.id` and `updatedAt`)
apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderSessionManager.ts:2524-2533 and :1066-1072 (the detach path captures every provider thread of the session with a non-empty roster)
apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:552-578 (the startup sibling writes the same whole-row events for every thread, so the side effect is not new in kind)
apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProviderTurnStartService.ts:646-651 (the code already notes that `activeProviderThreadId` 'flaps' when two live rows exist for one app thread)
apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/ProjectionStore.ts:3076-3091 (the read returns provider threads owned by the thread's nodes and subagents too)

apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/RunExecutionService.ts:680-684,794-801,1334-1344 (the finalization write re-emits `latestProviderThread` with its old roster; the ordering against the clear is racy on a `runtime_error` release with an active run)
packages/provider-muse/src/server/adapter.ts:694-707 (Muse task ids are native item ids; whether a replacement host reuses them is not visible here)
verdicts.scenario: An app thread has two provider threads bound to the same exclusive session, both with non-empty rosters. Examples are an older row left by rollback/fork, or a child row whose `appThreadId` is non-null. The session is released. `released` is built in projection order, so the last row written becomes `activeProviderThreadId`, and the thread's `updatedAt` is also reset to the clear time. If that last row is not the active one, the app thread points at the wrong provider thread. I could not confirm that Claude or Muse leave non-empty rosters on non-active provider threads of the same session, so this is unproven. Related race I also could not settle: on a `runtime_error` release during a running turn, the ingest fiber's failure finalization (RunExecutionService.ts:1334-1344) writes `latestProviderThread` with its stale roster. If that lands after the clear commits, the roster comes back and the thread stays Waiting.
verdicts.missing: Whether Claude or Muse can keep non-empty `pendingBackgroundTasks` on more than one provider thread of the same app thread and session, and whether such a row can be non-active or have a higher `first_run_ordinal` than the active row. Also the real ordering between the ingest fiber's failure finalization and the release's clear write.
